text:
Lane Hutson was first among 215 defensemen in Evolving-Hockey's wins above replacement last season, at 22, and he's picked up where he left off. Eighteen points in 18 games, a six-game point streak with eight assists, and Montreal takes 59% of the expected goals at five on five with him on, 13 points better than without him. TSN's Montreal radio had him as the best player on the ice in a recent game.

Nothing in this year's numbers looks inflated. His shooting is normal, the team's on-ice finishing is only slightly above expected, and his scoring rate sits inside our range. Evolving-Hockey did note last season ran a bit ahead of his chances, so the very top of his 2025-26 might be hard to repeat.

He carries the puck in on 54% of his entries (Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking) and gets to dangerous ice unusually often for a defenseman. His ice time is down nearly three minutes a night lately, worth watching. Our range: 64 to 90 points.
